applicabilityBasis.summary: Open USD is a U.S.-issued, dollar-pegged payment stablecoin issued by Bridge Building Inc. for payments, settlement and treasury use. Open Standard's launch disclosure specifies 1:1 USD mint and burn; Bridge's binding stablecoin terms provide redemption for one U.S. dollar, subject to user eligibility and compliance conditions.

genius.licensingRegulator: FinCEN MSB registration and applicable state money transmitter regulators for Bridge Building Inc. (NMLS #2450917). OCC preliminary conditional approval applies to the separate Bridge National Trust Bank in organization, not the current OUSD issuer.
genius.notes: Reviewed September 30 2026. Bridge's OUSD launch announcement expressly identifies Bridge Building Inc. as the current issuer and says Bridge National Trust Bank is a separate entity in organization, is not operational and does not issue OUSD. OCC Corporate Decision 1365 grants preliminary conditional charter approval to the proposed bank under Bridge Ventures LLC; it does not grant BBI a GENIUS payment-stablecoin issuer authorization. Bridge describes its compliance framework as GENIUS ready. The fetched Open Standard materials describe reserves maintained in compliance with U.S. regulatory requirements; a token-specific primary claim of GENIUS Act-compliant authorization was not verified. Issuer-announced-intent records Bridge's public positioning, with issuerPathway unknown rather than transferring the proposed bank's future federal pathway to BBI. No token-specific PPSI approval, state-qualified authorization or official GENIUS application was located. The broader DASP effective-date and offer/sale posture was not established by this token review, so it remains unknown. Bridge's live dashboard publishes OUSD supply, reserves and cash/Treasury allocation and identifies issuance from the US. Open Standard's September 30 launch announcement names BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY and promises monthly reserve attestations at that dashboard; Bridge's OUSD FAQ separately promises quarterly independently verified transparency reports. No OUSD independent report was available on the reviewed dashboard. These commitments do not establish a published monthly attestation. Bridge's binding terms require an eligible Bridge User for redemption, provide processing within two business days after compliance acceptance subject to factors outside Bridge's reasonable control, and deny holders a property interest in reserve assets. The launch announcement says Bridge charges no OUSD mint/redeem fees and imposes no liquidity restrictions delaying those transactions. MiCA out-of-scope is an issuer-distribution assessment based on Bridge's explicit EEA asset restriction and the absence of an OUSD EMT record or white paper in the reviewed register. Bridge Building S.A.'s EURR register entry and EU service-provider/EMI licensing do not authorize OUSD issued by BBI. Open Standard announces exchange distribution without regional eligibility details; EEA exchange admission remains an unresolved question and triggers reassessment if confirmed. No OUSD/BBI-specific public enforcement action was found in the dated, limited regulator-site searches; CD1365 discusses affiliate enforcement history and third-party allegations without identifying an OUSD action.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No OUSD/BBI-specific GENIUS PPSI approval, state-qualified authorization or official GENIUS application was located. Bridge's September 30 disclosure expressly rules out current OUSD issuance or GENIUS authorization through the proposed national trust bank. No OUSD-specific public enforcement action was located in the stated regulator-site searches; this is a bounded negative search, not a finding that no affiliate enforcement history exists. The reviewed ESMA EMT register contains Bridge Building S.A.'s EURR entry but no Open USD/OUSD record or white paper; Bridge explicitly restricts EEA stablecoin support to USDC and EURC. Announced exchange availability does not establish EEA admission.
